claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has a coercive field at or below approximately 100 Oe.
Introducing 1–3 at% nitrogen can preserve the single-phase fcc structure of FeCoNi.
Interstitial nitrogen incorporation creates localized lattice distortions in fcc FeCoNi.
The nitrogen-induced lattice distortions locally break cubic symmetry.
Nitrogen-induced distortion increases local magnetic anisotropy.
Interstitial nitrogen enhances the magnetocrystalline anisotropy of fcc FeCoNi.
Interstitial nitrogen creates additional domain-wall pinning sites.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy and additional domain-wall pinning raise the coercive field.
Nitrogen doping will raise the coercive field significantly above that of undoped fcc FeCoNi.
The coercive field may increase by a factor of approximately two to three relative to undoped fcc FeCoNi.
The nitrogen-doped alloy will retain high saturation magnetization.
The proposed coercivity enhancement is restricted to approximately 1–3 at% nitrogen while the fcc phase remains intact.
Excessive nitrogen doping may cause phase instability.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement depends on nitrogen concentration and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is explicitly bounded to nitrogen levels that retain the single fcc phase and acknowledges that excessive doping may cause phase instability, yet phase separation from excessive doping is declared sufficient to falsify the hypothesis. An outcome outside the stated structural/compositional boundary should not by itself falsify the in-boundary coercivity claim.
